subject: geography
title: Defining Globalisation
welcome_lead: Examine Friedman, Held and competing definitions.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on globalisation theory, Friedman, Held and historical waves.

concepts.def: Held (1999): widening, deepening and speeding up of worldwide interconnectedness.
Sees nation-state as obsolete; market integration triumphs (Friedman).
Regards globalisation as exaggerated; trade is mostly intra-regional (Hirst).
Sees major change but with national agency intact (Held).
Harvey's term for how technology shrinks effective distances.
Travel time reductions: Atlantic crossing took 6 weeks in 1750, 6 hours today.

walkthroughs.body_html: Friedman (2005) The World is Flat argues ICT and outsourcing have levelled the playing field. Held argues for a more nuanced flow-based view. Hirst and Thompson note that 80 percent of EU trade is intra-EU and FDI is concentrated, suggesting globalisation is uneven.

First wave: 1870-1914 trade liberalisation, gold standard (collapsed in WWI). Second wave: post-1945 Bretton Woods, container shipping (since 1956 reduced costs 90 percent). Third wave: 1990s onwards with ICT, China WTO entry (2001), supply chains.

David Harvey (1989) described how rail, steamships, jets, telegraph, internet successively reduced effective distance. London-Sydney: 6 months by sail (1850), 23 hours by 747 (2024). Email reduces communication to seconds. Geography of place reshaped.

mcqs.q: Why do TNCs locate production in LICs?
options: Because TNCs want to develop poorer countries and lift them out of poverty.
Outsourcing means moving to another country and offshoring means hiring contractors.
Lower labour costs, weaker regulation, access to raw materials, large potential markets, and government incentives like tax breaks in special economic zones.
Because LICs have better infrastructure than HICs.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between outsourcing and offshoring?
options: Outsourcing means moving to another country and offshoring means hiring contractors.
Because LICs have better infrastructure than HICs.

Outsourcing means contracting work to another company; offshoring means relocating work to another country. A firm can outsource without offshoring, or offshore without outsourcing (in-house overseas).
Outsourcing and offshoring are the same thing.

mcqs.q: What is the 'race to the bottom' critique of globalisation?
options: Because LICs have better infrastructure than HICs.
Race to the bottom is when companies offshore work to mines and underground factories.

The argument that TNCs play countries off against each other, relocating to those with lowest wages, weakest regulation and lowest taxes — pressuring governments to cut standards to attract investment.
The race to the bottom means TNCs compete with each other for the lowest prices.
